metaDescription: Margin Recovery Pilot, Core, and Control. 14-day discovery / action window with open-case verification. Prove recoverable margin on the stack you already run.

heroSupport: One defined financial scope. Prove Verified Value. Then grow.

how.title: Price follows the operating surface.
how.lead: Not seats. Not tokens. Not per-Decision credits.

pilot.title: 14 days to find and stage recovery.
pilot.lead: Uncover recoverable margin and prepare action. RADR keeps tracing open cases until value is applied or the case is closed.
pilot.body: One group or 2–3 locations. Supplier invoices, contracts, POS / menu where needed, AP evidence where available. Includes historical open credits / disputes / rebates when available — using evidence you already have.
points: Evidence package · recovery Trace · Verified Value

core.name: RADR Core

core.audience: Connect the operation. Make better Decisions. Verify what changed.

control.audience: Coordinate, approve and learn across the group.

enterprise.body: For larger groups we can scope SSO / SAML, custom RBAC, warehouse connections, custom APIs, security review, data policies, custom onboarding, dedicated support, SLA and multi-entity deployment.

compare.title: What changes as RADR takes on more.

items.a: Pricing depends on locations, operating scope and the level of Decision responsibility RADR takes on.
RADR is priced around the operation it covers, not the number of people who need access. Exact access and governance are scoped with the deployment.
No. RADR is designed to continuously watch the operating surface within the agreed scope. We do not want teams deciding whether an issue is worth a credit to investigate.
RADR is deployed against real operating data and designed to influence economically material Decisions. We begin with paid scoped deployments rather than a free self-serve tier.

items.q: Can we start with one location?
items.a: Yes. This is the preferred starting point for many deployments — often as a paid Pilot on one defined economic problem.

items.q: Do we need all our systems connected first?
items.a: No. Start with what you have. RADR expands as more systems and context come online.
Yes. RADR is designed to expand from one operating problem to locations and portfolios.

items.q: Can we start with only one economic territory?
items.a: Yes. Deployments can begin focused on BUY, LABOR, SELL or RECOVER — but RADR’s operating model is cross-domain by design. Value often comes from the relationships between territories.
Yes. Larger groups can scope advanced controls, security, custom integrations, SLA and multi-entity deployment under Control.

ready: Put one operating problem on RADR.
readyLead: Tell us what you run, where margin disappears, and which systems hold the evidence. We will scope the right place to start.
